To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the affordance and mirror system are best understood in terms two challenges faced by organisms: the selection among multiple affordances dependent on context and the exploitation of a hierarchical organization of behaviour.

1) the two challenges faced by organisms in the selection of affordances and the hierarchical organisation of behaviour can be solved by the same set of mechanisms and processes; 2) these mechanisms and processes are based on a hierarchical organisation of affordances and actions and their interactions; 3) the two challenges can be solved by two different sets of mechanisms and processes, which are not based on hierarchical organisation.

(a) The affordance and mirror neuron systems can be understood by analysing how organisms solve two key challenges, namely: the need to select the most appropriate affordance in a given situation and the need to organise behaviour hierarchically, (b) The affordance system can be modelled as an attentional system that selects the most appropriate affordances in a given context and the mirror neuron system can be modelted as a system that exploits the advantages of hierarchical organisation of behaviour.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a computational framework for affordance and mirror neurons, which can help to understand the mechanisms underlying the two systems and their interactions, as well as their role in human behaviour.
the study of affordances and their relation to the mirror system.
the study of how the brain deals with two fundamental challenges faced by complex animals: the selection among multiple affordances in the environment and the hierarchical organisation of behaviour.

a comprehensive account of affordance and mirroring systems should be able to explain how organisms select among affordances and how the hierarchical organisation of actions is exploited.

the mirror system and the affordance system are not two separate entities, but rather two complementary components of a single, integrated system.
